title: Customers with a poor payment track record by dollar value
prompt: For customers with a loan, compute what share of their total loan_payments dollar amount was paid on time. Which customers are below 50% — poor by value, not just by payment count?
population: Customers with at least one loan, and all loan_payments across their loans.
metricDefinition: sum(on-time loan_payments amount) / sum(all loan_payments amount), per customer with a loan; flagged when below 50%.
transformationPlan: sum loan principal per customer (for context)
sum on-time payment amount and total payment amount per customer, across all their loans
compute the on-time share by dollar value
referenceSql: WITH customer_loans AS (SELECT customer_id, sum(principal) AS total_principal FROM loans GROUP BY customer_id), payment_totals AS (SELECT l.customer_id, sum(lp.amount) FILTER (WHERE lp.status = 'on_time') AS on_time_amount, sum(lp.amount) AS total_payment_amount FROM loans l JOIN loan_payments lp ON lp.loan_id = l.loan_id GROUP BY l.customer_id) SELECT cl.customer_id, cl.total_principal, pt.on_time_amount, pt.total_payment_amount, pt.on_time_amount / pt.total_payment_amount AS on_time_share FROM customer_loans cl JOIN payment_totals pt ON pt.customer_id = cl.customer_id WHERE pt.on_time_amount / pt.total_payment_amount < 0.5

commonWrongAnswers.sql: SELECT l.customer_id, count(*) FILTER (WHERE lp.status = 'on_time')::DOUBLE / count(*) AS on_time_share FROM loans l JOIN loan_payments lp ON lp.loan_id = l.loan_id GROUP BY l.customer_id HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE lp.status = 'on_time')::DOUBLE / count(*) < 0.5
commonWrongAnswers.whyWrong: Measures the on-time rate by PAYMENT COUNT, not by dollar amount — a customer could make many small on-time payments and one huge missed one and still look fine here, which is exactly the by-value distinction the question asks for.
